app.title: {site} – candidates, constituencies and results 2026
app.description: Slovakia's 2026 local and regional elections: results by constituency, municipality and polling district, ballots by address, candidates with sourced notes.
app.features: Enter your address or click the map to see every ballot voted on there – mayor, municipal council, regional president and regional council – with the candidates in ballot order, their parties and the results of the 2026 elections: each candidate's votes and share, the winners and the turnout, on the ballots and on the map, down to the polling districts. The map also marks who holds each office now and with what share of the vote they won it in 2022, and for the candidates researched it adds notes on their career and controversies, each linked to its source. It covers every municipality and constituency in Slovakia, with no ads and no tracking.
help.how: Click a place on the map or search for an address, a municipality or a candidate. You will see every contest voted on there, with the candidates in ballot order. Click a candidate's number to circle it, as on the ballot: Favourites lists everyone you circle, to keep or to share. Shift+click the number, or double-tap it, to cross the candidate out instead: the list then mutes them, as the filter does. A party's tag or a mark adds it to the filter the same way: a click shows only those candidates, Shift+click or a double tap hides them.

about.title: About {site}
about.purpose: {site} shows every constituency of the Slovak municipal and regional elections of 24 October 2026 on a map, with the candidates standing in each. It is meant to help voters make their own decisions.
about.disclaimer.title: Disclaimers
about.method.title: How it works
about.method.candidates: The MV SR candidate lists carry no municipality codes, so municipalities are matched by name within their okres (district). Candidacies of one person in several contests are merged by municipality, name and age.
about.method.map: The map is drawn directly from the ZBGIS municipal boundaries at several levels of detail, without a base map from other servers. The regional council constituencies and the city council constituencies of Bratislava and Košice consist of whole municipalities and city districts, as set by the decisions of the regions and cities. The countries around Slovakia are drawn coarser, from Natural Earth, for orientation only. The faint roads, railways, rivers and lakes under the colours, also for orientation only, come from OpenStreetMap, simplified for each zoom.
about.method.addresses: The address search uses the MV SR address register. Addresses whose point lies more than 100 m outside their municipality are shown without a location.
about.method.obvody: Municipalities with one council constituency have it assigned directly. Municipalities and city districts with several constituencies define them in their own resolutions, by streets, house numbers or parts of the municipality. An AI agent transcribed these resolutions from the municipalities' websites into rules, which were checked to put every address of the municipality into exactly one constituency; the resolutions are linked below. Where a resolution has not been processed yet, all constituencies are shown. The number of seats comes from these resolutions; a council with one constituency whose 2026 number is not known yet shows the number elected in 2022 (Statistical Office of the Slovak Republic), labelled as such.
about.method.approximate: The boundaries on the map are simplified and meant for orientation. The boundaries between the constituencies within a municipality are drawn around the houses that belong to them (dashed: approximate) and smoothed into plausible areas, so a few houses may lie in the area of a neighbouring constituency; the address search gives the constituency of the address itself. A few municipalities have published only the names of their constituencies (such as the lower and upper end of the village), not which houses belong to them; their constituencies are our estimate from the map, and their ballots say so.
about.method.incumbents: Who holds an office now was rebuilt from the final results of the 2022 elections and of every municipal by-election since (Statistical Office of the Slovak Republic) and matched to the candidates by municipality or region, name and age. Substitutes who took up a vacated seat and departures without a by-election are missing, and a candidate whose surname changed is not matched, so the chair mark (“holds this office now”) may be incomplete. How each office holder won the seat comes from the same final results, counted in the unit where the seat was won: the municipality for a mayor, the region for a regional president, the council constituency of that election (or the whole municipality if it had one) for a councillor. The share for a mayor or president is of the valid ballots; for a council, where each voter could vote for several candidates, it is of the voters with a valid ballot, so the shares of one constituency add up to more than 100 %. The share of all registered voters and the turnout (voters who took part, of those registered) are given too.
about.method.research: Candidate research: for each candidate, AI agents search the sites on the list below, separately for each research language (sources in Slovak, in Hungarian and so on), decide which pages are about the candidate rather than someone with the same name, and report each relevant fact as a finding: a one-sentence claim, a verbatim quote and the page it comes from. Findings are sorted as career, serious controversy (charges brought by the police or prosecutors, a court decision against the candidate or another serious matter an authority has established) or allegations and disputes (claims the candidate denies or no one has confirmed, cases that ended in the candidate's favour, and lesser matters); in doubt, a finding goes among the allegations and disputes. Every research result first says what was searched (which sites, and when) and only then what was found; nothing found there is no proof that nothing exists. A candidate not researched yet is marked as such: no research has been done on them.
about.method.research_check: Every page cited is downloaded and kept, and a finding is accepted only if its quote appears word for word in the kept copy and the page names the candidate; the copy is linked next to the original. The claims are written by artificial intelligence and no one checks them one by one; a quote in a language other than that of the interface comes with a machine translation that no one has checked. The research covers only the sites on the list and may miss things: finding nothing does not mean there is nothing.

about.allowlist.title: Sources for candidate research
about.allowlist.intro: AI agents researching candidates may cite only these sites and their subdomains:
about.research.title: Research coverage
about.research.unresearched: Candidates not counted here have not been researched yet: no sources have been searched about them.
about.category.official: Official sites and public registers (plus the official sites of municipalities and regions)
about.allowlist.rule: Media selection rule: in each country, brands are ranked by online weekly reach in the Reuters Institute Digital News Report 2026; those with a net trust (trust minus distrust) of at least +5 points are kept and the top ten are taken (fewer where fewer brands qualify); on equal reach, higher net trust wins. Ukraine is not covered by the report, so the Institute of Mass Information's High Quality List (first half of 2026) is the credibility filter there; sites with a reach figure in the Internews Ukraine 2025 survey come first. Slovak media in Hungarian are the news sites measured in the Forum Minority Research Institute's 2021 survey of Hungarians in Slovakia, ordered by readership.
about.allowlist.exclude: Sections with user-generated content are excluded: sites with “{hosts}” in their host name and pages with a “{paths}” segment in their path.
about.allowlist.blocklist: Sites on the konspiratori.sk list are always blocked, even if they match the list above (snapshot of the list from {date}, sites: {n}):
